problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $L$ given that 

$$
L[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors of a Matrix Using the Properties of Diagonalization

examples.worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $E\mathbin{:}$ 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069457/assets/9dee992fa1cc903eb23299b52080a7ebba31ef550bb22c4938c45939e8541be4.png)

Therefore, $E$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $E$ are $\lambda_1=3$ and $\lambda_2=6$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P.$ Computing $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P={[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{-3}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & 2 \\ \frac{1}{3} & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069457/assets/23dd5ab30b31bf85d84f290fdf9c71529cfd753b98688149f103980894ad91c6.png)

feedback.worked_solution:
We have been given the following diagonalization of $M.$

$$
M={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt[8]{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt[4]{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

So, since $M=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${M}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{M}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the inverse of the matrix $P.$ We get

$$
{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}^{16} & =P{D}^{16}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt[8]{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt[4]{2}\end{aligned}]}^{16}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}(\sqrt[8]{2})^{16} & 0 \\ 0 & (\sqrt[4]{2})^{16}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{4}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 48 \\ 4 & 32\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-32 & 72 \\ -24 & 52\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
